answer: You can starve a sybil farm by front-loading its costs. Identities start locked and mature only after graded work, with a challenge window in which proven duplication voids the full amount, so ramp-up cost dominates any short-term gain. In effect the orchard of free entry disappears, the pigment of a fake identity has to be posted in advance, and the echo case is a farm that funds its own destruction. Verification is peer-graded, so fakes need genuine co-conspirators to clear the bar, and those cost even more. That flips the unit economics: authentic agents get cheaper while duplicates.
